---
title: "Acquisition Workflows"
format: gfm
---

The application separates control, blocking acquisition, and display work so
that a slow plot cannot silently become the measurement clock. The practical
consequence is that each hardware data path has an explicit owner.

## Ownership at a glance

| Activity | Hardware/data path owned | Can run alongside |
|---|---|---|
| Scope live viewer | Isolated viewer connection | Scope DMA preview supplied by the DMA owner |
| Scope file DMA | Scope DMA buffer | MCA histogram; independent channels where supported |
| Current IIR | Input-filter direct reads on a worker-owned connection | Scope viewing/recording and MCA, subject to firmware resources |
| Current DMA | Scope DMA buffer plus periodic Scope acquisition | No other Scope DMA on that channel |
| MCA histogram | Pulse-processor accumulation | Scope activity |
| MCA list-mode/PSD | MCA list-mode buffer and pulse processor | Scope activity; bounded subscribers may share accepted event batches |
| Coincidence | Two MCA list-mode streams and shared software start | Scope activity; no separate MCA DMA owners on those channels |

Stop the current owner and wait for its worker to finish before starting a
conflicting operation. A checkbox changing state is not proof that a native IIO
buffer has already been destroyed.

## Scope

The Scope workspace supports live raw and persistence views, trigger-level and
pretrigger markers, periodic/level/edge trigger modes, frame length and gap,
and analogue DAC baseline control.

Recommended workflow:

1. With acquisition stopped, run **Auto Setup** or load known trigger and DAC
   calibration values.
2. Confirm polarity and channel identity in the live raw view.
3. Set frame length, pretrigger, trigger mode, and frame gap.
4. Use the draggable trace/markers for preview, then verify the next hardware
   frame after the setting is committed.
5. For a file capture, choose a new destination and start DMA. Existing files
   are not silently overwritten.
6. Stop before reconfiguring geometry or handing Scope DMA to Current.

Scope Auto Setup can provisionally search for narrow, randomly arriving pulses
when a forced-frame survey contains only baseline. Its measured DAC sensitivity
makes vertical drag previews meaningful; without it, the preview is only an
approximation.

The direct-IIO DMA path accepts complete frames only. It arms the blocking
reader before enabling acquisition and stops the core before draining and
destroying the buffer. See [Capture Files and Integrity](data_formats) for the
NDMA v1 layout limitation on IP122 periodic geometry.

## Current

Use IIR mode for a lightweight scalar trend and Scope DMA mode for raw waveform
coverage and sample-weighted statistics. The modes expose different raw
signals and require their own calibration. The full workflow, callback example,
and performance diagnostics are in [Live Current Monitoring](current_monitor).

## MCA histogram and debug data

MCA control covers low-pass, CR-RC², trapezoid, CFD, charge-comparison, and PSD
zero-crossing settings, plus a 16,384-bin spectrum and debug waveform bank.

Configuration writes are synchronized with non-DMA acquisition. Changing DSP
settings while the histogram is running performs a controlled stop/write/restart
and begins a new accumulation; stale histogram and elapsed-time presentation
state is cleared. Do not reconfigure the pulse processor during list-mode DMA,
because that requires the complete buffer stop/drain/close/rearm lifecycle.

Histogram chunks are transferred sequentially and are not an atomic snapshot
while acquisition is running. Stop acquisition before using a final histogram
as a stable result.

## MCA list mode and PSD

Choose the list-mode output under **Settings → DMA Settings...**:

- binary NDMA;
- appendable HDF5;
- ROOT `TTree`;
- online-only (no file).

Binary, HDF5, and ROOT retain records whether or not live PSD is enabled.
Charge Comparison can feed the live PSD view through its own bounded subscriber;
the subscriber cannot steal batches from recording. Online-only events without
a consumer are intentionally discarded.

Current IIO list mode uses fixed 16 KiB frames containing 1,024 opaque 16-byte
records. Low event rates can therefore delay a live update until a complete
frame is available or the acquisition stops and drains. End-of-run driver
counters and the run summary determine whether continuity was verified.

## Coincidence

Coincidence is a two-channel list-mode workflow, not an extension of the MCA
histogram viewer. It owns both list streams, energy gates, timing rules, shared
start, and optional paired files. Use the dedicated
[Coincidence Measurement](coincidence) guide before changing its timing schema
or interpreting pair counts.

## PSU, global diagnostics, and external instruments

Per-channel IDS/HV is available only when its converter and temperature devices
are present. Global diagnostics cover board-wide sensors and shared trigger
state. Optional Modbus instruments are discovered through the configured
ser2net bridge.

The application performs safe acquisition and power-supply shutdown on close.
Scripts that enable HV must provide their own `finally` cleanup and must not
assume that closing a DPP-only connection controls an external supply.
